This shop leads with 四色 at ¥2,000 — four soba in one order: さらし, 抹茶 (green tea), 胡麻 (sesame) and a seasonal one. Flavoured soba is made by working matcha, sesame or citrus peel into the dough, and because those additions weaken it the dough generally needs MORE binder, not less — so the coloured noodles a menu presents as the refined choice are, if anything, the more wheat-bearing ones. Nothing here publishes a ratio either way. ⚠ AND ONE ITEM IS BOTH NOODLES AT ONCE: うどん蕎麦合盛 at ¥1,200 serves soba and UDON on the same tray, which removes any doubt about wheat being in the kitchen. ⚠ THE PLATES WORTH KNOWING ABOUT: 板わさ (¥1,200) is fish cake, which is a quiet wheat item; こんにゃく味噌田楽 (¥850) is konnyaku, a plant, under miso; アボカド山葵 (¥850) is avocado and wasabi and is the closest thing here to a clean plant dish; and 蕎麦がき at ¥2,000 is buckwheat paste rather than noodles, which is the one form of soba with no dusting flour on it — worth asking about even though the ratio question remains.

tokyo_vegan_eat_tokyo.price_note: ⚠ THIS IS THE ONLINE SHOP, NOT THE RESTAURANT BOARD — the stored website is a BASE storefront selling retort packs, so the four products below are what the shop mails out, not what it plates. No in-restaurant menu or price was found. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ AND IT CONTAINS THE SHARPEST SINGLE ILLUSTRATION OF THE TWO-AXIS PROBLEM IN THIS ENTIRE DATASET. The flagship product of a shop called VEGAN EAT TOKYO is its ヴィーガンカレー — and its own allergen line reads 小麦、カシューナッツ、大豆: WHEAT, cashew, soy. A vegan curry with wheat in it. Meanwhile the other product, ひよこ豆のトマト煮, is explicitly described as グルテンフリー. So within one vegan kitchen, the headline dish is closed to a coeliac and the second dish is open — and nothing about the word "vegan" predicts which. This is the asymmetry the dataset exists to record: plant-based is not wheat-free, the two restrictions are independent, and a shop can be scrupulous about one while the other is simply not the question it was answering. ⚠ THE CASHEW IS WORTH FLAGGING SEPARATELY: vegan kitchens use cashew constantly as a dairy substitute — for cream, cheese and sauce bodies — so a NUT allergy is a live and under-anticipated risk at exactly the restaurants a plant-eater is steered toward. It is named here in black and white.

It also notes that coffee and tea are served. Several lines are marked 期間限定 (limited season) or 数量限定 (limited quantity) and those markers are carried into the notes below, because a 5,500円 three-grape parfait that exists for a few weeks is not the same fact as a standing 1,400円 banana parfait. ⚠ A FRUIT PARLOUR LOOKS LIKE THE EASY CASE FOR BOTH DIETS AND IS NOT. A Japanese parfait is built in a glass in layers, and the layers under the fruit are the problem: whipped cream and ice cream are dairy in every one of these, and sponge, cornflake and wafer/biscuit layers are standard construction in this style of parfait. The shop does not publish a per-item build, so every line below is dairy — vegan 'no' — and every line is an open question on wheat rather than a safe one. ⚠ THE HONEST SUMMARY IS THAT THE FRUIT IS THE SAFE PART AND IT IS NOT SOLD SEPARATELY ON THIS PAGE; the parlour also runs a fruit counter and an online store, which is where an unassembled option would be, not here.

tokyo_abura_soba_kasugatei_shi.price_note: EMPTY BECAUSE THE MENU IS A PICTURE. 油そば 春日亭's chain site has an お品書き page whose entire content is a single JPEG, images/contents/oshinagaki.jpg, with no alt text, no HTML list and no price anywhere in the markup. The only machine-readable sentence on it is an exclusion notice: 「※担々油そばに関しまして、魚介メニューの提供に伴い、中野店、神田店ではお取り扱いがございません」 — the tantan abura soba is not sold at the Nakano and Kanda branches because of their seafood menu. That footnote does NOT name 渋谷店 or 渋谷センター街店, so it does not restrict this shop. The chain lists 23 branches including both 渋谷店 and 渋谷センター街店. ⚠ WHAT IS CERTAIN WITHOUT READING THE IMAGE, BECAUSE IT IS THE NAME OF THE SHOP: ABURA SOBA IS A WHEAT NOODLE. 油そば is a brothless ramen — thick wheat-and-kansui noodles tossed with a soy-and-oil tare at the bottom of the bowl — so every bowl on that card is wheat twice over, from the noodle and from the tare, and the 割スープ that is poured in at the end is a meat or fish stock. There is no version of this dish that is not wheat. Recorded empty for the prices; the gluten answer needs no image.

tokyo_nikujiru_suigyoza_gyopao_2.price_note: EMPTY BECAUSE THE MENU IS A PICTURE, INCLUDING THE ENGLISH ONE. The branch's own site has four menu-ish pages — menu, course, 'Food & Drink / English edition' and an all-you-can-eat gyoza buffet page — and the English-edition page, which is the one that sounded most promising, turns out to be two scanned JPEGs of a printed card (grandmenu英語_page-0001.jpg and _page-0002.jpg) with no alt text and no HTML list behind them. Recorded empty for the prices; the gluten answer needs no image. Worth returning to with OCR since a printed English card exists.

tokyo_trois_bagues_vertes.price_note: ALMOST EMPTY: THE SHOP'S SITE HAS NO MENU PAGE AT ALL. troisbagues.com's navigation is HOME / トロワバグについて / アクセス / ギャラリー / オンラインショップ / ブログ / お問い合わせ — there is no menu item in it, and the site even leaks a PHP warning (`Undefined variable $onepage_menu` in header-home.php) where a menu section would sit, which suggests the template once had one. No food or drink price appears anywhere. What the shop does publish about itself: a small 喫茶店 opened in 1976 (昭和51年) that ages its green beans before roasting — エイジングコーヒー, 熟成豆, オールドビーンズ — and brews by NEL DRIP; it offers a wine selection to taste, ships beans nationwide, and its gallery captions say 「軽食もございます」 (light meals are available) and 「ワインやビールもございます」 without naming a single one. It also runs a monthly wine gathering. 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-12-1 富田ビルB1, tel 03-3294-8597, one minute from Jimbocho A5; Mon–Fri 10:00–20:00 (L.O. 19:30), Sat and holidays 12:00–19:00 (L.O. 18:30), closed Sundays. ⚠ ONLY ONE PRODUCT IS NAMED ANYWHERE ON THE SITE — トロワブレンド, the house blend built on its old beans — and it is named in the ONLINE SHOP block, i.e. as a bag of beans to buy rather than as a cup served at the counter. It is recorded below on that basis and unpriced, which is why this record is provisional/low. ⚠ THE 軽食 IS THE REAL GAP: a Showa-era kissaten's light meals are toast, sandwiches, pilaf and spaghetti nearly without exception, all of which would be wheat, but the shop names none of them and that must not be filled in from the pattern.

tokyo_style_s_cakes_co.price_note: PARTIAL, AND THE REASON IS A REAL DISTINCTION FOR A VISITOR. The only priced list Style's Cakes publishes is its WHOLE-CAKE ORDER card (cakes.php), and the shop states on that page 「(店頭ではカットしたピースのケーキのみの販売となります。)」 — over the counter it sells cut slices ONLY. So a walk-in customer cannot buy anything below at the price shown; these are 21cm and 24cm whole cakes for pre-order, and the shop asks for roughly three days' notice on 03-3291-6910 (「3日前までを目安にして頂けるとご希望のケーキをお作りできます」). The per-slice counter prices are NOT published anywhere on the site, and the shop.php gallery is images only with no text. The seasonal windows in brackets are the shop's own. ⚠ GF/VEGAN REALITY: this is a tart-and-pie boutique, so pastry is the whole product — every item below sits in or on a wheat crust, and the two 21cm/¥7,000 items that are not tarts are a pie and a banana-cream tart. Nothing here is a candidate for a coeliac, and the shop publishes no allergen information at all. The quiche is listed because it is on the same order card, not because it is any safer.

tokyo_ban_thai.price_note: NO MENU COULD BE READ, AND THE REASON IS THE PLATFORM RATHER THAN THE SHOP. The site for タイ国料理 バンタイ is built on STUDIO (studio.site), a Nuxt single-page app that ships an empty HTML shell and paints the page from JavaScript. curl and WebFetch both return only the site title and a STUDIO banner. This tick went further than a fetch: STUDIO publishes each site's content as a snapshot JSON in Google Cloud Storage, and the app's own __NUXT_DATA__ payload names the exact path. That snapshot was retrieved and parsed — and its "components" key is an empty object, so the text simply is not in the published payload this egress can reach. Menu subpaths (/menu, /food, /drink) were probed as well and either 404 or return the same shell. This is a COMPLETE result for a text-only harvest: the shop may well display a full menu to a real browser, but nothing was found that could be quoted, and nothing has been guessed. A future pass with a headless browser that executes JavaScript is the way to finish this record; a re-fetch will not be. NOTE ON THE SUBPATH PROBE: unlike the other STUDIO sites in this batch, ban-thai.studio.site returns HTTP 200 for /menu, /food and /drink — but all three are byte-identical to the top page (14,949 bytes each), i.e. an SPA catch-all, not real pages. Do not record that as a menu page existing. ⚠ FOR A COELIAC, Thai cooking is one of the higher-yield cuisines in Japan because rice noodles and rice are the staples — but it is also one where fish sauce, oyster sauce and soy sauce are used constantly, and Japanese-market oyster and soy sauces carry wheat. Nothing about this specific kitchen was established.

tokyo_nouka_no_daidokoro_shinj.price_note: ⚠ THE WEBSITE IN THIS DATASET NOW POINTS AT SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY, AND SOMEONE SHOULD FIX THE RECORD. https://www.noukanodaidokoro.shop/ redirects to noukanodaidokoro.shop and serves a GERMAN-LANGUAGE RECIPE BLOG. Its front page is a list of posts titled "Das perfekte Currywurst Sauce Rezept", "Königsberger Klopse Rezept", "Jägerschnitzel DDR Rezept", "Hähnchenflügel im Ofen knusprig", "Gambas al Ajillo Rezept" and so on, under a masthead reading "Noukano" with Impressum and Über uns links. The .shop domain has been dropped by the restaurant and re-registered as SEO content. There is no Japanese text, no address, no menu and no connection to 農家の台所 anywhere on it. THIS IS WORTH FLAGGING BEYOND THIS RECORD: a stale website field that resolves to unrelated food content is exactly the kind of source that could get a fabricated menu written against it by a less careful pass — the page is full of dish names and would look plausible to anything that did not read the language. Nothing from it has been used. 農家の台所 新宿三丁目店 is recorded as a vegetable-forward izakaya, which would make it one of the more promising vegan candidates in Shinjuku; it needs a fresh first-party URL before that can be checked.

Nothing on the card is labelled vegan and the two things closest to it (ニンジンマリネ, ポテトフライ) are unstated on dressing and fryer.

tokyo_hasegawa.price_note: ⭐ THE MOST USEFUL FACT HERE IS A PRICE ANOMALY: THE SET MEAL COSTS LESS THAN THE CUTLET ALONE. ロースカツ定食 is 900円 and includes rice, soup and cabbage; 厚切りロースカツ on its own is 1,300円. The 400円 gap is not a discount, it is a different and thicker piece of pork — but a reader scanning the list will see a 900円 full meal sitting under a 1,300円 single item and should understand which one is the bargain and why they are not the same cut. The 串揚げ6本 at 1,050円 sits between them. ⚠ TONKATSU IS PANKO AND PANKO IS BREAD. There is no version of this shop that works for a coeliac: every one of the three items is crumbed in wheat breadcrumbs and deep-fried, the 串揚げ share the fryer, and the sauce poured over tonkatsu is a Worcester-style sauce that itself normally contains wheat. Two separate wheat sources, batter and sauce, before the cabbage is dressed. Nothing is meat-free either — ロース is pork loin, and 串揚げ at a tonkatsu counter is a mixed skewer set whose contents are not published, so even the vegetable skewers in it share oil with pork and usually prawn. ON THE LISTING: three items, no 更新日, undated. Lunch only — 11:30–14:00, closed Sundays and public holidays — and 13 seats, 10 of them at the counter, at 花川戸2-7-3. A thirteen-seat lunch-only counter in Asakusa means queueing.

items.en: Thick-cut pork loin cutlet, à la carte — the premium cut, sold without the set
items.note: ⚠ パン粉＝小麦。とんかつソースも小麦を含むのが一般的。PORK loin in wheat breadcrumbs, deep-fried, and the sauce it is served with is normally wheat-containing too. Note this costs 400円 MORE than the full set meal below, because it is a thicker cut — not because the set is discounted.

⚠ 衣＝パン粉＝小麦。中身は非公開。Wheat crumb again. The shop does not publish what is on the six skewers, which matters: kushiage sets conventionally mix pork, prawn and vegetables, so this is simultaneously an undeclared-allergen risk (PRAWN) and useless to anyone avoiding meat, since the vegetable skewers are fried in the same oil.

items.en: Pork loin cutlet set — cutlet with rice, miso soup and shredded cabbage
items.note: ⚠ PORK, wheat crumb, wheat sauce. Worth knowing what else is on the tray: the 味噌汁 is made with dashi, so it is FISH, and the cabbage arrives with a dressing that is usually sesame or a soy-based one. A set meal multiplies the number of undeclared things on the table rather than reducing it.
